name: The Woodwright's Shop
description: The Woodwright's Shop is a traditional woodworking show hosted by Roy Underhill on the Public Broadcasting Service in the United States. It is one of the longest running "how to" shows on PBS. Since its debut in 1979, the show has aired over 400 episodes. The first two seasons were broadcast only on public TV in North Carolina; the season numbering was restarted when the show went national in 1981. It is still filmed at the UNC-TV studios in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina.

videos.title: Maul & Glut
videos.overview: Watch Roy make two traditional tools by first felling a tree then shaping a maul and glut using period iron woodworking tools.

videos.title: Shaving Horse
videos.overview: Learn how to make a shaving horse – one of the most important hand-tool shop fixtures for working with drawknives and spokeshaves.

videos.title: Shaving Horse Part 2
videos.overview: Learn how to make a shaving horse – one of the most important hand-tool shop fixtures for working with drawknives and spokeshaves.

videos.title: Hay Rake
videos.overview: Spend time with Roy as he shows you how to build one of his favorite projects: a hickory hay rake that is both strong and lightweight.

videos.title: Lathes
videos.overview: Join Roy on a tour of the history and development of human powered machines, including one of his favorites: the lathe.

videos.title: Rocking Chair
videos.overview: Learn how to build a classic armless rocking chair using traditional tools and techniques. Then create a woven white oak seat for the rocker. Plus, watch as Roy’s guest Bryant Holsenbeck demonstrates how to weave a traditional basket.

videos.title: Rocking Chair Part 2
videos.overview: Learn how to build a classic armless rocking chair using traditional tools and techniques. Then create a woven white oak seat for the rocker. Plus, watch as Roy’s guest Bryant Holsenbeck demonstrates how to weave a traditional basket.

videos.title: Log Cabin
videos.overview: Watch as Roy demonstrates the steps and hand-hewn joinery used in building traditional log cabins.

videos.title: Timberframe Construction
videos.overview: Watch and learn as Roy addresses the details of timber framing, including post-and-beam and mortise-and-tenon construction techniques.

videos.title: Dough Bowls and Pitch Forks
videos.overview: Watch as Roy makes a pitchfork and a dough bowl, each from a single piece of wood.

videos.title: Blacksmithing
videos.overview: Spend some time at the forge with Roy to learn basic blacksmithing techniques and discover how to create a spike dog (a tool used in timber framing).

videos.title: Panel Frame and Dovetail
videos.overview: Follow along as Roy discusses frame-and-panel construction for doors, and the basic steps for cutting a dovetailed joint.

videos.title: Colonial Williamsburg
videos.overview: Travel with Roy to Colonial Williamsburg to take a look at 18th-century craftsmanship including a visit with a wheelwright, a cooper and a blacksmith, as well as a look inside the Anthony Hay Cabinet Shop.

videos.title: Getting a Grip on It
videos.overview: Watch as Roy examines a number of tool handles, then creates an axe handle from a split of hickory and turns a chisel handle.

videos.title: Candle Stand
videos.overview: Follow along as Roy walks you through the steps of creating a classic walnut candle stand.

videos.title: Plane Truth, Version 1
videos.overview: Learn the history of a wide variety of handplanes as Roy explains their many and specialized uses.

videos.title: Plane Truth, Version 2
videos.overview: Learn the history of a wide variety of handplanes as Roy explains their many and specialized uses. Lost episode.

videos.title: Getting Into Drawers
videos.overview: Join Roy as he makes a hand-hewn, half-blind dovetailed drawer for his workbench, and discusses many of the techniques used in traditional drawer making.

videos.title: Finding and Fixing
videos.overview: See what Roy discovers at a scrap yard, antique store and flea market on his way to “The Woodwright’s Shop.”

videos.title: Cutting your Teeth
videos.overview: It’s all about staying sharp, and in this episode Roy examines the dizzying array of saws available, from familiar panel saws to bowsaws and pit saws. Plus, as a special bonus Roy shows you how to sharpen a bowsaw.

videos.title: While the Iron’s Hot
videos.overview: Accompany Roy on a visit to Colonial Williamsburg to work with the living history museum’s blacksmiths as they make a froe, and forge a cant hook.

videos.title: Straight and Narrow
videos.overview: Lost episode.

videos.title: Vernacular Sash
videos.overview: Roy takes us through the hand-crafted creation process of a sash-style window, explaining the stiles, rails and muntins.

videos.title: Woodwright at Sea
videos.overview: The evolution of modern boat building in America starts with simple designs such as those found in rough-hewn canoes – and its surprisingly fundamental. Watch Roy explore how to build a boat as he visits the Hampton Mariner’s Museum and discusses boat building that’s large and complex. There is a clear evolution in tools and techniques and it’s both instructive and entertaining to watch this process.

videos.title: Tale of Two Toys
videos.overview: Roy looks at a collection of classic wood toys, and then shows us the steps to create a Crow Chaser.

videos.title: Inner Woodworking
videos.overview: Observe as Roy looks at the mechanics of wood and how a trees’ growth affects how you work wood once you have it in your shop.

videos.title: Workbench (Part I)
videos.overview: Roy hand-crafts the frame for a massive, classic workbench using pegged and keyed mortise-and-tenon construction.

videos.title: Workbench (Part II)
videos.overview: Roy finishes the workbench started in the previous episode.

videos.title: Cooper’s Bucket
videos.overview: With some help a couple of coopers from Colonial Williamsburg, Roy shows the steps to creating a cooper’s bucket.

videos.title: Blanket Chest
videos.overview: Follow along as Roy builds a stunning nailed-together, six-board blanket chest with an interior till.

videos.title: Simple Gifts
videos.overview: Watch and learn as Roy builds three simple gift projects, including a flapping duck toy, a small pine knock-down bench and a wooden egg beater.

videos.title: Whimsy Diddling
videos.overview: Join Roy as he walks you through the process for making a Gee Haw Wimmey Diddle, a quintessential mountain folk toy, along and a willow whistle.

videos.title: Furniture Carving
videos.overview: Watch as Roy’s guest Colonial Williamsburg’s Wallace Gusler talks about the techniques and tools needed for carved furniture.

videos.title: Whetstone Quarry
videos.overview: Take a trip with Roy through the geological history of whetstones, then head out on a hunt for rough materials to make your own whetstone for sharpening.

videos.title: The Gunsmith
videos.overview: Spend time with Roy and gunsmith Gary Brumfield of Colonial Williamsburg as they discuss the steps to making a handcrafted 18th-century-style rifle.

videos.title: Wood for the Weaver
videos.overview: Discover details about some of the traditional wooden implements used by weavers, including spinning wheels, clock reels and niddy noddys; and watch as Roy makes a swift and a tape loom.

videos.title: The Luthier
videos.overview: Join Roy in learning the techniques and processes used to create a violin in the 18th century.

videos.title: The Basket Makers
videos.overview: Watch as Roy Black and Robert Watson show Roy how to make round-bottom and flat-bottom white oak baskets, starting from a log and using only hand tools.

videos.title: The Dominy Shop
videos.overview: Roy takes us on a tour the Dominy Shop at Winterthur Museum. The shop holds the tools and shop items used by three generations of craftsman from 1750-1850.

videos.title: A Spring Pole Lathe
videos.overview: Roy walks us through the steps to create a simple, but accurate and functional spring pole lathe.

videos.title: Ball & Claw Feet
videos.overview: Roy welcomes Wallace Gusler from Colonial Williamsburg, and he shows the process to create a cabriole leg with a ball and claw foot.

videos.title: The Wainscot Chair
videos.overview: Roy works with his daughter, Rachel, to create a child-size, 17th-century chair found in a book by Wallace Nutting.

videos.title: Tool Boxes & Chests
videos.overview: Roy explores the contents of a recently purchased tool chest, trying to determine something of the original owner. He then shows how to recreate the chest itself.

videos.title: Chip Carving
videos.overview: Mack Headley from Colonial Williamsburg visits the shop and demonstrates the chip carving techniques used to decorate furniture.

videos.title: Good Fences
videos.overview: Roy looks at the details of early-American fences, including lightweight and portable fences used for sheep herding, garden fences and more substantial post and rail “fences” used in forts built around 1620.

videos.title: Kitchen Gifts
videos.overview: Roy shows you how to make some always-gift-appropriate and useful utensils for the kitchen including a rolling pin, heavy spoon, a collapsible drinking cup and more.

videos.title: Raising the Shop
videos.overview: Roy pitches in with the raising of the frame-and-timber structure for Anderson’s Forge at Colonial Williamsburg.

videos.title: Building a Boat
videos.overview: Roy builds a small rowboat using traditional tools and techniques.

videos.title: Rittenshouse Hygrometer
videos.overview: After discussing how humidity affects different wood species, Roy makes a clever and simple late 18th-century hygrometer to measure the humidity in the shop.

videos.title: Corner Cupboard
videos.overview: Roy recreates a classic pine corner cupboard.

videos.title: Highchair
videos.overview: To celebrate his new nephew, Roy builds an 18th century baby’s high chair with rush seating.

videos.title: Rustic Rockers
videos.overview: Roy starts off the “Making Things From Nature” season by giving us some history of rustic furniture and walks through the steps necessary to make a Rustic Rocker.

videos.title: Bark Bottoms
videos.overview: To finish up the Rustic Rocker, Roy takes us into the woods to gather hickory bark, and then heads into the shop to create the woven bark seat for the rocker.

videos.title: Baby Cradle
videos.overview: Roy takes us into the shop to finish up a pilgrim-style oak cradle that he started, but never finished, reviewing the “tricky” parts necessary to create the whole project.

videos.title: Chris' Workshop
videos.overview: We visit with a 14-year-old traditional woodworker who sells his wares (walking sticks, toys and more), to make more money to buy tools he can’t make for himself.

videos.title: Iron Machine, Foot Power
videos.overview: A collector of cast-iron, foot-powered woodworking lathes and fret saws visits with Roy and they try out a number of the machines.

videos.title: Hutch Table I
videos.overview: In part one, Roy starts the base of a classic early-American project that serves as a tilt-top table, chair and storage unit.

videos.title: Hutch Table II
videos.overview: In part two, Roy finishes the base and completes the top of the early-American tilt-top table. He also shows how to make a traditional milk paint finish for the piece.

videos.title: Iron Bloomery
videos.overview: Roy visits with David Harvey, a Blacksmith at Colonial Williamsburg, and learns how to turn bog ore into a woodworking chisel.

videos.title: Berry Buckets, Sussex Trugs and Bark Sheaths
videos.overview: Roy shows how to create three projects that are created directly from trees and bark, with very little refinement.

videos.title: Wheelwright
videos.overview: We head back to Colonial Williamsburg where Roy visits with master wheelwright Dan Stebbins to discover the mysteries and realities of making wheels for early American wagons and carts.

videos.title: Music Mill
videos.overview: Roy makes a six-note music mill from wine bottles that is powered by hand crank (but can also be powered by a water wheel).

videos.title: Secrets From the Cabinet Shop
videos.overview: Roy travels back to visit with master cabinetmaker Mack Headley at the Anthony Hay shop at Colonial Williamsburg. He shares some of the secrets that were standard fare for 18th century American woodworking.

videos.title: A Glass Act
videos.overview: Sash joinery, or making windows, is the ultimate test of organizational skills, and Roy takes us through the many steps and details that must align to make a good window.

videos.title: Turning of the Screw
videos.overview: Traditional woodworking required making much of your own tools and machinery, and the wooden screw is a major component in those. Roy looks at the making of wooden screws for use in the shop.

videos.title: That Old Spoon Carver
videos.overview: Roy visits with expert spoon carver Roger Sandstrom to talk technique, wood selection and more about carving spoons and treenware.

videos.title: Don't Crush That Bookstand, Hand Me the Pliers
videos.overview: Roy tackles creating a classic Wooden Pliers whittled from a single piece of wood, and then expands the concept to a folding bookstand using similar joinery.

videos.title: Folding Lathe
videos.overview: Roy shows how to build an 18th Century French lathe designed to fold up and store in the corner.

videos.title: Jacobian Stool
videos.overview: We learn how to create the traditional joinery for a Jacobean stool.

videos.title: Turning and Carving
videos.overview: Roy finishes the Jacobean stool by adding the turning and carving to the frame.

videos.title: Things They'd Never Make for Themselves
videos.overview: We spend some quality time with Roy making small projects from scrap wood, including wooden ties, a pop gun, ado-nothing machine and a flying top.

videos.title: Anderson's Forge
videos.overview: Roy travels to the John Anderson Forge at Colonial Williamsburg to look at how nails, hinges and tools were made in Colonial America.

videos.title: Botetourt Chair
videos.overview: Roy takes a look at 18th Century woodworking details found in furniture from the Colonial Williamsburg cabinet shop.

videos.title: Shaker Lap Desk
videos.overview: Build one of the classic 18th Century projects with Roy; a Shaker lap desk.

videos.title: Rachel's Wagon
videos.overview: Roy walks through the steps required to build a wooden wagon for his daughters – but manages to have some fun himself.

videos.title: Toolmaker's Art
videos.overview: Roy visits with Peter Ross at the Anderson Forge to look at 18th Century tool making, in particular, a gentlemen’s hatchet.

videos.title: House Framing Doggie Style
videos.overview: Only the best for Roy’s pooch, Grit: a brick and Tudor framed doghouse is this episode’s project.

videos.title: Noveltails
videos.overview: Roy takes a look at the design and benefits of many traditional dovetails used in woodworking, then goes even further to look at some more unusual dovetails.

videos.title: Longer and Stronger
videos.overview: When you need a longer board (or rafter), then a traditional scarf joint may be the answer. Roy discusses the history, value and creation of this important joint.

videos.title: Country Comfort
videos.overview: Roy shows us the steps to create the perfect outdoor chair — the Adirondack.

videos.title: Shaker Boxes
videos.overview: After a look at a number foot-powered woodworking machines, Roy and his guest show how to use a few of the machines to make traditional Shaker oval boxes.

videos.title: Bookcaseology
videos.overview: This episode is Roy’s version of waste-not, want not. He shows how to build a coffin-shaped bookcase so that the materials involved aren’t wasted, but used during life — and after.

videos.title: Woodwork, Needlework
videos.overview: Blending two traditional crafts, Roy builds an adjustable needlework stand or French design.

videos.title: Whirligigs
videos.overview: Whirligig expert Andy Lundy stops by the shop to talk about the history, design and construction details of a variety of whirligigs.

videos.title: Felling and Hauling
videos.overview: Traditional woodworking starts with the trees. Roy shares the traditional steps necessary to fell a tree and get the wood into the shop.

videos.title: Bramble Work
videos.overview: Roy gives us a look at rustic Bramble Work furniture. He then creates a small table in this style, working with twigs fastened in geometric patterns.

videos.title: Farmwood
videos.overview: Roy works through the varied historical uses of lumber. For use in construction, furniture, heating on your own farm, and for sharing with others. No part of the tree is wasted.

videos.title: Old South Homestead
videos.overview: On a trip back to the Underhill homestead, Roy takes us on visit of some of the construction details used in building the 1850’s house and outbuildings.

videos.title: Gameboards
videos.overview: Roy shows us how to make a couple of classic board games: Fox and Geese; and a checkers (or chess) board.

videos.title: Woodcut Printing
videos.overview: We travel to the Book Binders Shop at Colonial Williamsburg to learn the history and reality of woodcutting for use in printing.

videos.title: African Legacy
videos.overview: Roy looks at a balaphone (or marimba), kalimba (or thumb piano), a banjo and couple of African drums.

videos.title: Turning the Tables at the Tavern
Make a Music Mill From Bali
Boat to Build With the Kids
Make a Chair
videos.overview: (Part 1) — Roy starts a classic post-and-rung rocking chair using traditional greenwood techniques.

videos.title: Rollin' on the Rocker
videos.overview: (Part 2) — Work on the rocker continues; shaping the tenons, boring the mortises and creating the splats.

videos.title: Splittin' and Sittin'
videos.overview: (Part 3) — Work on the rocker is completed with the creation of the rockers and adding a hickory bark seat.

videos.title: Hewing a Dough Bowl
videos.overview: Roy creates a traditional dough bowl from tulip poplar.

videos.title: Wood-Turning Tricks
videos.overview: Eleanor Underhill joins Dad in the shop to turn a painted candle stand.

videos.title: Archer's Bow
videos.overview: Roy welcomes a bowyer and a fletcher to the shop to make a woodland Indian’s bow and river cane arrows.

videos.title: Four-Poster Bed
videos.overview: This may not be the four-poster bed you’re thinking of, as Roy builds a rustic version from rough, red cedar logs

videos.title: Blacksmith of Williamsburg
videos.overview: Roy visits Colonial Williamsburg to watch the creation of a set of hardware for window shutters.

videos.title: Williamsburg Woodcraft
videos.overview: Continuing the Williamsburg theme, Roy visits the woodworker’s shop to watch frame-and-panel shutters made

videos.title: Woodworker's Grab Bag
videos.overview: Daughter Rachel joins Roy in the shop to make a marble track toy and Kick-Me machine.

videos.title: Thomas Jefferson, Woodworker
videos.overview: Roy visits Monticello to look at some of the architectural creations and innovations of the former President..

videos.title: Dovetailed Bookcases
videos.overview: Roy recreates stacking “book box” shelves built to Thomas Jefferson’s specifications, and still on display at Monticello.

videos.title: Japanese Woodcrafter
videos.overview: Toshio Odate visits the shop to discuss and demonstrate Japanese woodworking tools, techniques and joinery.

videos.title: Bentwood Boxes of the Northwest Coast
videos.overview: Roy visits Gregg Blomberg and explores woodworking traditions of the Pacific Northwest.

videos.title: A Civil War Quilting Frame
videos.overview: Roy is joined by his wife, Jane, to build a traditional quilting frame.

videos.title: African Chair From the Ivory Coast
videos.overview: Roy and his friend Robert Watson make a “man’s chair” using tools from the Ivory Coast of Africa.

videos.title: Hispanic Furniture-Making
videos.overview: Roy learns about northern New Mexico woodworking on the Santa Fe Trail.

videos.title: Colonial Tape Loom
videos.overview: Roy begins making a tiny tape loom, used for making decorative fabric.

videos.title: Dovetailing a Loom Box
videos.overview: Roy finishes the tape loom by making a beautiful box for it with dovetails and turned columns.

videos.title: A Colonial Standing Desk
videos.overview: Roy makes a standing desk using mortise-and-tenon and tongue-and-groove joints.

videos.title: Banding Together
videos.overview: Instrument maker Marcus Hanson makes inlay banding with Roy at the Anthony Hay Cabinet Shop.

videos.title: The Art of Finishing
videos.overview: Roy returns to the  Anthony Hay Cabinet Shop to learn finishing.

videos.title: Fifteen Tools From a Dead Man's Chest
videos.overview: Roy restores the tools found in an antique chest.

videos.title: A Pilgrim Chest of Oak
videos.overview: Roy makes a Spanish pilgrim’s chest from New Mexico.

videos.title: Woodcarvers of the Sacred
videos.overview: Returning to New Mexico once again, Roy explores religious carving and woodworking in the mountains north of Santa Fe.

videos.title: Moravian Chair
videos.overview: Roy makes a Moravian chair that’s reinforced with dovetailed battens, which make this small piece extraordinarily strong.

videos.title: English Walnut Music Stand
videos.overview: Build a beautiful music stand that adjusts for height and angle to best suit the musician.

videos.title: Fair And Square
videos.overview: Roy works through the steps to turn a round log into a square timber, and then shows how to bore a square hole.

videos.title: Hickory Pitchfork
videos.overview: Through shaving, steaming and bending, Roy creates a pitchfork from a green hickory limb.

videos.title: Continental Army Canteen
videos.overview: Learn to build a wooden canteen using stave construction.

videos.title: Make A Windsor Chair (Part 1)
videos.overview: In this three-episode project Roy builds a variation of a swiveling Windsor chair allegedly used by Thomas Jefferson during the writing of the Declaration of Independence.

videos.title: Make A Windsor Chair (Part 2)
videos.overview: In this three-episode project Roy builds a variation of a swiveling Windsor chair allegedly used by Thomas Jefferson during the writing of the Declaration of Independence.

videos.title: Make A Windsor Chair (Part 3)
videos.overview: In this three-episode project Roy builds a variation of a swiveling Windsor chair allegedly used by Thomas Jefferson during the writing of the Declaration of Independence.

videos.title: The Geddy Foundry of Williamsburg
videos.overview: Roy visits the foundry at Williamsburg to view the processes of pouring and finishing brass and silver for hardware and household items.

videos.title: Crazy Wooden Things for Kids to Make
videos.overview: Roy uses the theme of string-powered toys to show us how to make a spinning top, pump drill and a simplified version of the mechanism for a flying ball clock.

videos.title: Spiral Turning and Xylophone Tones
videos.overview: Learn the basics of two simple and fun projects: carving a spiral and building a tongue drum.

videos.title: Norwegian Wood
videos.overview: Roy visits Lillehammer, Norway looking at traditional Norwegian folk architecture and building techniques.

videos.title: Timber Building in the Land of the Midnight Sun
videos.overview: Still enjoying his trip to Norway, Roy visits a Viking ship museum and the Norwegian Folk Museum.

videos.title: Woodworkers of the Red Dragon
videos.overview: Roy visits a recreated Celtic village in Wales, looking at Welsh woodworking including building construction, clog making and traditional carved Welsh love spoons.

videos.title: The Carpenter's Tool Box
videos.overview: Learn to build Roy’s iconic carpenter’s tool tote.

videos.title: Ancient Woodcraft of Ireland
videos.overview: Roy looks at Irish woodworking, including houses, harps, caravans and traditional ship-building techniques.

videos.title: A Sailor's Sea Chest
videos.overview: Learn to build a sailor’s sea chest with beveled through dovetails.

videos.title: Oak High Stool with a Hickory Bark Seat
videos.overview: Roy builds a stool starting with splitting and riving the green wood and ending with a woven-bark seat.

videos.title: Standing Embroidery Shop
videos.overview: Learn the steps to build a standing embroidery hoop large enough to handle embroidery on a quilt.

videos.title: The Timber-Frame House
videos.overview: Roy builds a scaled model of a Welsh cruck-frame barn, teaching the woodworking principals of timber framing.

videos.title: Wooden Lock and Key
videos.overview: Create a clever wood lock-and-key door set in the shop with Roy.

videos.title: Shaker Sewing Stand
videos.overview: Roy builds a traditional single-drawer Shaker sewing stand.

videos.title: Panel-Frame Construction
videos.overview: Learn the benefits and uses of frame-and-panel construction and the joinery steps to create a frame-and-panel door.

videos.title: Tools of the Eighteenth Century
videos.overview: Roy visits Colonial Williamsburg to view their exhibit of 1,500 eighteenth-century woodworking tools.

videos.title: The Williamsburg Blacksmiths
videos.overview: Watch a traditional woodworking tool –a drawknife –forged using historically accurate techniques.

videos.title: Blacksmiths Forge Ahead!
videos.overview: Learn the steps used to smith a Suffolk door latch used during colonial times.

videos.title: Sharpening Tools
videos.overview: Roy builds a cedar box for an old sharpening stone while simultaneously teaching you the principles of sharpening and how to maintain the edges on the tools he uses. He also discusses the differences between various kinds of sharpening stones.

videos.title: Jefferson's Walking-Stick-Chair
videos.overview: Roy shows you how to make a walking stick-chair – a walking stick that folds out to become a small chair – much like the one used by Thomas Jefferson as he laid out plans for the University of Virginia.

videos.title: Chisels, Gouges and Mallets
videos.overview: Roy explores the wide, and sometimes strange, world of chisels. You’ll learn more about the tools you work with every day, and see how to use odd tools from history that you’ve likely never seen.

videos.title: Trestle Table
videos.overview: Roy makes a “sawbuck” trestle table – first delving into the interesting details, and then actually building it.

videos.title: Wooden Schoop Shovel & Spoons
videos.overview: Starting with a raw popular log, Roy splits, chops, cuts and carves a huge wooden shovel. Along the way you’ll go through nearly every aspect of woodworking, from rough to fine work.

videos.title: The Wooden Boat School
videos.overview: Roy travels to the Wooden Boat School in Brooklyn, Maine. See three distinct approaches to traditional boat building taught by three different instructors at the school

videos.title: The Marionette Makers
videos.overview: Roy arrives to find his shop taken over by a gaggle of marionette puppets! We’re joined by a pair of professional puppeteers that demonstrate how to build three types of puppets.

videos.title: Folding Workbench (Part 1)
videos.overview: Start learning to make a simple, yet sturdy, portable folding workbench.

videos.title: Folding Workbench (Part 2)
videos.overview: Finish learning how to put the workbench together, plus add all-important workholding features.

videos.title: Candle Stick Maker
videos.overview: Make a colonial threaded candle stand – the screw threads allow you to finely adjust the height and position of the candles.

videos.title: Adirondack Woodcraft
videos.overview: Visit the shores of Blue Mountain Lake in Adirondacks – see how to make an Adirondack guide boat and an Adirondack pack basket. Plus see the region’s signature furniture.

videos.title: Williamsburg Trunk Maker
videos.overview: Visit the harness shop of Jim Clatter in Colonial Williamsburg. Learn how to make a variety of leather items including a knife holster, pistol buckets and water buckets using 18th-century techniques.

videos.title: Climbing a Colonial Steeple
videos.overview: Roy climbs Bruton Parish Steeple in Williamsburg, Virginia, which has been holding a bell since the 1770s. See details of the original construction that tell us about how our ancestors lived, worked and thought.

videos.title: Arts and Crafts Bookcase
videos.overview: Learn the steps to recreate a knock down bookcase originally built by the Roycrofters of East Aurora, New York.

videos.title: The Secret Dovetailed Box
videos.overview: Roy shows how to make a small box using a hidden dovetail joint that looks like a miter joint when complete.

videos.title: Wood Inlay
videos.overview: This episode starts by making a scratch stock tool necessary to create the grooves for the simple Holly inlay that follows.

videos.title: The Giant Chisels of Gaul
videos.overview: Roy visits local blacksmith shops and museums in the Alsace region of France in search of a giant chisel.

videos.title: Roll Top Cabinetry
videos.overview: Using a roll-top joinery process, Roy creates a small box with tambour doors.

videos.title: African Drum
videos.overview: Roy shows how to build an “African” drum that originally came from colonial America.

videos.title: Woodcraft of Alsace, France
videos.overview: Roy continues his visit to the Alsace region looking at woodworking and timber-building traditions.

videos.title: Comb-Back Windsor Chair, Part 1
videos.overview: In this two-part project, Roy shows the steps to create a classic comb-back Windsor chair.

videos.title: Comb-Back Windsor Chair, Part 2
videos.overview: In this two-part project, Roy shows the steps to create a classic comb-back Windsor chair.

videos.title: Sand-Powered Wooden Toys
videos.overview: Roy builds two simple toys: an interlocking-joint puzzle; and a sand-powered whirligig.

videos.title: Cutting the Knuckle-Hinge Joint
videos.overview: Learn to create the useful knuckle-hinge joint and, just for fun, whittle a wooden pair of pliers.

videos.title: Making Wooden Screws
videos.overview: Roy shows how to use a tap and screw box to create wooden screws for use in shop and furniture projects.

videos.title: The Pencil People
videos.overview: Learn the history of writing instruments and the evolution of the pencil, then look at a variety of pencil sharpeners from the past.

videos.title: Make Your Shaving Horse
videos.overview: Roy shows you how to make a shaving horse from a single 2x10.

videos.title: Whittling Chains and Ball in Cage
videos.overview: Learn to whittle the mysterious, impossible-seeming wooden chain and ball-in-cage.

videos.title: Windsor High Chair
videos.overview: Roy make a child’s Windsor highchair showing classic Windsor techniques.

videos.title: Chinese Bamboo Chair
videos.overview: Make a chair out of grass ... Chinese bamboo, that is.

videos.title: Shaker Boxes
videos.overview: Make a No. 3 bentwood Shaker box – a deceptively simple design.

videos.title: Panel-Framed Bench
videos.overview: Roy’s panel-framed bench has a storage space built beneath the seat.

videos.title: Hanging Bookcase

videos.overview: Secrets of the mysterious two-screw vise revealed! Chris Schwarz joins Roy Underhill to rediscover this enigmatic wooden vise.

videos.title: Screw Cuttin’ Lathe
videos.overview: Make your own darn metal screws with this 1889 foot-powered lathe! Roy shows how to cut perfect threads, cones and tapers in iron and brass.

videos.title: The Troublesome Triangle Stool
videos.overview: The old triangular stool spells trouble for Peter Follansbee and Roy Underhill as they tackle a trio of terrible turned tenons!

videos.title: Wretched Ratchet Reading Rack
videos.overview: With foot-powered lathes, Peter Follansbee and Roy Underhill turn this adjustable bookstand from walnut and maple.

videos.title: Raising Panel-Zona
videos.overview: Make raised panels for your doors with care and flair! Roy Underhill uses both complex planes and tricks with basic tools to raise the classic panel.

videos.title: Carving the Camellia
videos.overview: Woodcarver Mary May makes basswood flowers bloom. Get in the groove of high-relief carving with sharp gouges and good-grained wood!

videos.title: Forging the Hold Fast
videos.overview: Haul out the anvil and forge this essential bench tool! Blacksmith Peter Ross shows how to forge historical versions of this powerful gripper.

videos.title: The Enfield Cupboard
videos.overview: Make this Shaker cabinet and dwell in utopian serenity! Simple to construct and elegant in design, this cupboard is a standby in any room or shop.

videos.title: The Shaker Bend
videos.overview: What made these American communal craftsmen tick? From their furniture to their bentwood boxes, the Shakers may be our most modern artisans.

videos.title: Rachell's Standing Desk PT. 1
videos.overview: Give your butt joints a break with the tenons and dovetails that connect this pine standing desk from Pennsylvania.

videos.title: Rachell's Standing Desk PT. 2
videos.overview: The miter-clamped breadboard end makes a broad desktop that always stays flat.

videos.title: The Venerable Bead
videos.overview: Roy Underhill demonstrates how to cut bead moldings with hand planes for corners that look sharp and last longer.

videos.title: Carving Away With Mary May
videos.overview: Classical carver Mary May provides a lesson on woodcarving and a proper rebuke for edge tool abuse!

videos.title: Swinging Saw Vise
videos.overview: Roy duplicates the beveled bridle joints and chamfered chops of an old saw-sharpening vise.

videos.title: Sharpen That Saw!
videos.overview: Using giant model rip and crosscut saws, Roy demonstrates how to correctly sharpen handsaws.

videos.title: Combination Planes
videos.overview: Roy attempts to replace a chest of molding planes with one complex metal contraption

videos.title: Joined Chest With Peter Follansbee
videos.overview: The master joiner of Plimoth Plantation shows how to frame a small, mortised, and tenoned chest in the old English style.

videos.title: Paneled Chest With Peter Follansbee
videos.overview: A master joiner shows Roy how to make and fit the beveled panels and storage till into a framed chest from the Pilgrim era.

videos.title: Early Iron With Peter Ross
videos.overview: Master blacksmith Peter Ross shows how to forge iron hinges and locks from the earliest days of the American experience.

videos.title: Try Square with Christopher Schwarz
videos.overview: Chris Schwarz shows Roy how to measure up with an English try square based on the examples in the famous Benjamin Seaton tool chest.

videos.title: Dutch Tool Chest with Christopher Schwarz
videos.overview: Learn to make the simple and useful Dutch tool chest with its characteristic 30-degree slanted lid.

videos.title: Big Ash Mallet!
videos.overview: With ash head and hickory handle, Roy shows how to make a proper joiner's mallet for the ages.

videos.title: Taming the Timber Bench
videos.overview: Your legs will stay tight in this classic German carpenter’s bench built with stopped sliding dovetails.

videos.title: Pinch Rods and Squeezy Blocks
videos.overview: This pair of sliding diagonal rods with copper collars will help you get your chests square and your dovetails tight.

videos.title: Tapered Tail Tripod Table 1
videos.overview: Walnut legs riven from the log begin this table inspired by the Dominy workshops.

videos.title: Tapered Tail Tripod Table 2
videos.overview: A walnut burl top and tricky turning makes tapered dovetails for a three-legged table.

videos.title: Viceless Devices
videos.overview: From the holdfast to the birdsmouth, Roy explores wondrous ways to grip the grain and rediscovers and old trick from a rare book.

videos.title: Daring Diagonal Dovetails
videos.overview: Learn to cut the rising diagonal dovetail for corners that are stronger and striking, no matter how you look at them.

videos.title: Shop Class Tabouret
videos.overview: The old shop-class plant stand joined with half-laps and dowels teaches us to pay attention to the grain, not just the machine.

videos.title: Campaign Furniture
videos.overview: Christopher Schwarz shows the ins and outs of Campaign furniture made for travel to the far-flung reaches of the Empire.

videos.title: Fitting Brass
videos.overview: Chris Schwarz shows how to fit brass corners and hardware flush with the surfaces of Campaign furniture.

videos.title: The Crotch and the Horse
videos.overview: An old shaving horse from the Virginia mountains demonstrates that the natural shapes in timber make the strongest wooden construction.

videos.title: Dovetail Saw
videos.overview: Tom Calisto joins Roy to make a brass-backed hand saw perfect for the finest dovetails or the toughest tenons.

videos.title: Tempered Steel
videos.overview: Blacksmith Peter Ross shows how to forge, weld, harden and temper tool steel for cutting edges that stay sharp longer.

videos.title: Woodwright! - The Musical
videos.overview: The Underhill Rose band joins Roy in the shop for a musical misadventure in the ways of the Woodwright.

videos.title: Rocky Bentwood Cradle I
videos.overview: Part 1 of 2. A rocking cradle modeled after one spotted in the Grand Bazaar of Istanbul is crafted in the Season 35 premiere.

videos.title: Rocky Bentwood Cradle II
videos.overview: Conclusion. A rocking cradle is completed with pine sides and rockers. A lathe-turned carrier bar joins it all together.

videos.title: Stamp Out Cookie Carving!
videos.overview: Woodcarver Mary May joins Roy to carve springerle cookie molds for every occasion.

videos.title: Double Drawer Shaker Table
videos.overview: How to cut the mortise and tenon joints for the legs and frame of a Shaker table.

videos.title: Groovers and Shakers
videos.overview: The dovetailed and grooved construction techniques found inside Shaker drawers are detailed.

videos.title: Turning Shaker Knobs
videos.overview: Cherry knobs for Shaker furniture are turned on a foot-powered lathe. Also: finishing a joined table top.

videos.title: Cross Cut Conundrum
videos.overview: How to use a cross-cutting wood saw.

videos.title: Bowl Carving with Peter Follansbee
videos.overview: Master craftsman Peter Follansbee joins Roy to hew huge bowls from poplar & sycamore wood.

videos.title: Hollows & Rounds
videos.overview: These most basic molding planes also prove the most versatile as we look at making and using wooden hollows and rounds.

videos.title: Welsh Stick Chair I
videos.overview: Roy makes this country cousin of the Windsor chair using the same tools and techniques.

videos.title: Welsh Stick Chair II
videos.overview: The challenge of the Welsh stick chair continues as Roy shapes spindles and backs for a proper sit-down.

videos.title: Tool Smithing with Peter Ross
videos.overview: Dividers, calipers and turning tools take shape as master blacksmith Peter Ross shows Roy the art of tool-making.

videos.title: Plain Pine Box
videos.overview: Roy looks into the simplest form of furniture, the plain pine box.

videos.title: Van Gogh's Chair
videos.overview: The Season 36 premiere shows how to make a chair similar to the one portrayed in Vincent Van Gogh's masterpiece.

videos.title: Sliding Lid Boxes
videos.overview: Roy shows how to create easy-to-make wooden gift boxes with mitered corners and lids that slide in grooves.

videos.title: Carved Oak Desk Box
videos.overview: Master of Pilgrim-century furniture Peter Follansbee joins Roy to make a slope-lidded, carved box from carved white and red oak.

videos.title: Waving Arm Whirligigs
videos.overview: Figures from history including Benjamin Franklin and Muhammad Ali inspire Roy’s new line of waving arm wooden whirlygigs.

videos.title: Wedged Tusk Tenon
videos.overview: Roy and workbench builder Will Myers test out the strength of the classic wedged mortise and tenon joint for take-apart furniture.

videos.title: Swedish Shrink Box
videos.overview: Woodworker Peter Follansbee shows Roy Underhill how to make Swedish shrink boxes from hollowed wood with inserted bottoms.

videos.title: Saw Like a Butterfly!
videos.overview: The great poet-athlete Muhammad Ali inspires the best lessons in woodworking – Saw Like a Butterfly, Plane Like a Bee!

videos.title: Firewood Carrier
videos.overview: Chair-maker Elia Bizzarri shows Roy how to make a split oak firewood carrier inspired by the classic wooden harvest rake.

videos.title: Double Casement Window
videos.overview: Roy Underhill makes a double, swinging casement window using wooden planes and premium pine.

videos.title: Roman Work Bench
videos.overview: Christopher Schwarz & Roy unlocks the secrets of the ancient Roman woodworker’s bench.

videos.title: Staked Furniture
videos.overview: A plank with inserted legs becomes a chair, a table, or a bench...

videos.title: Tool Chest Hinges & Latch
videos.overview: Tool Chest Hinges & Latch

videos.title: Tool Chest from Bristol
videos.overview: Roy shows how to dovetail a stout, sloped top tool chest.

videos.title: Who Wrote the Book of Sloyd?!
videos.overview: Sloyd, the late 19th century Swedish system of learning woodworking was intended to develop skilled, industrious, and morally upstanding citizens. We’ll give it a try, and hope it’s not too late for us!

videos.title: Holly Wood Spectaculars!
videos.overview: Steve Latta shows how to create decorative veneer patterns using oval engines, sharp knives, and patient perfectionism.

videos.title: The Roubo Bookstand!
videos.overview: One piece of walnut makes a beautiful bookstand as we follow the formula of an old French master.

videos.title: Rise of the Machines
videos.overview: Why do it by hand – when you can do it by foot? Roy Underhill gets caught up in up a bevy of century-old, foot-powered woodworking machines.

videos.title: Hand Plane Essentials With Chris Schwarz
videos.overview: Learn how to make gleaming surfaces, tight joints and crisp moldings through perfect planing.

videos.title: Big Ash Mallet!
videos.overview: Make a proper joiner’s mallet and you’ll never be lonely again! With ash head and hickory handle, Roy shows how to make a mallet for the ages.

videos.title: Carving Away with Mary May
videos.overview: Classical carver Mary May gives Roy his first lessons on woodcarving – along with a proper rebuke for edge tool abuse!

videos.title: Dovetailed Grease Pot
videos.overview: Walnut and boxwood make a little box with a secret lock to stash the woodworker’s pal.
